title: Declining Max Roach and Bird's wish to hire him
summary: He turned down Max Roach's call after Clifford Brown's death, and Louie Bellson says Parker wanted him for a band days before he died.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Didn’t you get a call to replace Clifford Brown?
Yeah. As a matter of fact that’s when I’d just started working The Lighthouse. Because Clifford died when, in ‘55 or 6.

Something like that. I was working The Lighthouse and I was doing well on the coast, and when that accident happened, Max Roach called me and wanted me to come work with the band. And I couldn’t leave town. I’d just established myself there pretty well, and I couldn’t leave, so I had to turn it down. I don’t know whether I’m sorry I did. As things worked out, they worked out pretty good. You know I just found out something not too long ago. I am rehearsing now with Louie Bellson. He’s doing a big band album next week in L.A., which, the rehearsals, they really sound great. Anyway Louie Bellson told me right before Charlie Parker died that he had talked to Charlie Parker and he said, “You know I’m sort of getting myself straightened out now.” They were together, I don’t know where it happened. But he said, “I’m trying to get myself straightened out and I want to get a band together. I want you on the band.” And he said, “You know Conte Candoli?” And Louie says, “Yeah.” And he says, “Well could you get in touch with him — I’d like to get him on the band too.” This is right, two or three days before he died.
Yeah. He wanted to get himself together, and the fact that he mentioned me, man, just I mean I’m just elated.
That’s a great thing to learn.
